title: Artificial Intelligence-Guided Prediction of Dental Doses Before Planning of Radiation Therapy for Oropharyngeal Cancer: Technical Development and Initial Feasibility of Implementation.
summary: Original full text develops a learned model to predict dental doses before treatment planning and tests feasibility against subsequent accepted plans in nine prospectively evaluated patients. The clinical dose estimation result is narrowly preliminary and not an outcome-benefit claim.
ai_technology: A learned model predicts dental radiation doses from planning inputs and is compared with accepted treatment-plan doses.
organization: Department of Radiation Oncology, University of California, San Francisco, California

evidence.tested: Original full text develops a learned model to predict dental doses before treatment planning and tests feasibility against subsequent accepted plans in nine prospectively evaluated patients. The clinical dose estimation result is narrowly preliminary and not an outcome-benefit claim.
evidence.unknown: Results are limited to the reported models, cohorts, datasets or experiments; broader generalization and clinical or operational benefit were not established.
